markets: Sells fuel cells to bus, truck, rail and marine makers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Fuel cell technology firm with transport customers; F1 could showcase hydrogen and advanced propulsion technology to engineering and industrial buyers.

name: BKV Corporation
desc: Produces natural gas in the Barnett Shale in Texas and Marcellus in Pennsylvania, with power generation and carbon capture projects.
markets: Sells gas to utilities and marketers in the United States; no international operations.
rationale: US gas producer with commodity sales and no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship has little commercial logic.

name: CNNC Huineng
desc: Clean energy arm of China National Nuclear Corporation that develops, builds and operates wind, solar and other renewable energy projects.
markets: Based in Beijing; projects assumed to be in China. No verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: State-owned power developer with no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak despite the Chinese Grand Prix.

name: Energo-Pro
desc: Owns hydropower plants and electricity distribution networks in Georgia, Bulgaria and Turkey, supplying retail and industrial customers.
markets: Hydropower and distribution assets in Georgia, Bulgaria and Turkey serving retail electricity customers; Czech-headquartered.
rationale: Regulated distributor and hydro generator with regional customers; limited brand marketing culture makes F1 a weak fit.

name: ENTEK
desc: Makes lithium-ion battery separators used in electric vehicles and energy storage, and is building a factory in Terre Haute, Indiana.
markets: Manufacturing in the United States for battery makers, with a new Indiana plant supported by a government loan.
rationale: Industrial battery materials supplier with business customers; F1 technology showcase has limited value for its audience.

name: Global Power Generation
desc: Electricity generation business in energy and renewable energy, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Based in Canberra; assumed to operate in Australia. Identity and international activity are not verified.
rationale: Identity unconfirmed and little known about products or customers; F1 fit cannot be established from available data.

name: Lincoln Electric
desc: Makes arc welding equipment, consumables and cutting systems for fabricators, automotive and shipbuilding customers, under brands including Harris Products.
markets: Manufactures and sells welding products across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions to industrial customers.
rationale: Global industrial brand with engineering and motorsport-relevant customers; F1 could support technology showcase and B2B hospitality.

name: Promigas
desc: Colombian holding company that transports and distributes natural gas through pipelines and utilities such as Surtigas and Gases del Caribe.
markets: Pipelines and gas distribution on Colombia's Caribbean coast, plus interests in gas distribution in Peru.
rationale: Regulated gas holding with regional customers; limited consumer branding and no Colombian race make F1 a weak fit.

name: Qcells
desc: Designs and makes solar modules, storage and projects, including a large panel factory in Georgia; US arm of Hanwha Qcells.
markets: Sells solar modules and systems in the United States, Europe, Asia and Australia; parent is South Korean.
rationale: Solar brand with residential and utility customers; F1 could support brand building in the US, Europe and Asia.

name: San Miguel Electric Cooperative
desc: Operates a lignite-fired power plant in Atascosa County, Texas, supplying member-owner electric cooperatives in South Texas.
markets: Sells power to member cooperatives in South Texas only; no international operations.
rationale: Member-owned coal-fired generator with no brand marketing needs; F1 sponsorship has no commercial rationale.

name: Seatrium
desc: Builds and repairs offshore platforms, floating production units and vessels; formed in 2023 from Sembcorp Marine and Keppel Offshore.
markets: Yards in Singapore, Brazil and other countries serving oil, gas and offshore wind customers worldwide.
rationale: Offshore engineering group with business customers; Singapore Grand Prix offers B2B hospitality, but consumer brand value is minimal.
changed: Formed in 2023 by merger of Sembcorp Marine and Keppel Offshore and Marine

name: Societatea Nationala Nuclearelectrica
desc: State-controlled nuclear power company operating the Cernavoda plant, whose two CANDU reactors supply about a fifth of Romania's electricity.
markets: Sells electricity in Romania; developing new reactors with international partners. Customers are in Romania only.
rationale: State-controlled single-site generator with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship has little commercial purpose.

name: Suniva
desc: Makes crystalline silicon photovoltaic solar cells in the United States, and brought the Section 201 solar trade case.
markets: Manufactures in Georgia, United States, for US module makers; no international operations known.
rationale: Small US solar cell maker with business customers; F1 fit is weak.

name: Ukrenergo
desc: State-owned national electricity transmission operator running Ukraine's high-voltage grid, dispatching power and managing interconnection with European networks.
markets: Operates Ukraine's grid and interconnections with European networks; customers are Ukrainian power market participants.
rationale: State grid operator in wartime; F1 sponsorship is not realistic or relevant.

name: Xcel Energy
desc: Provides electricity and natural gas to about 3.7 million electric and 2.2 million gas customers across eight US states.
markets: Regulated customers in eight central and western US states; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated US utility with local customers; F1 sponsorship holds little commercial purpose.

name: ACEN
desc: Ayala Corporation's energy platform developing and operating wind, solar, hydro and geothermal projects in the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia and elsewhere.
markets: Plants in the Philippines, Vietnam and Indonesia, with further projects in Australia and India.
rationale: Listed Asian renewable platform with expansion plans; Singapore Grand Prix offers regional corporate hospitality, but consumer marketing need is small.

name: Aethon Energy
desc: Private natural gas producer focused on the Haynesville Shale of East Texas and Louisiana, among the largest private US producers.
markets: Sells gas to US utilities and LNG buyers from the Haynesville; no international operations.
rationale: Private US gas producer with commodity sales and no consumer brand; Circuit of the Americas offers Texas hospitality only.

name: Aspen Aerogels
desc: Makes aerogel insulation such as Pyrogel and Cryogel for oil, gas and industrial pipes, and PyroThin barriers for EV batteries.
markets: Sells to energy industry and electric vehicle makers, including General Motors, in North America and other regions.
rationale: Materials technology firm with automotive battery customers; F1 could showcase thermal management technology to carmakers and engineers.

name: BNZ Energy
desc: Independent power producer that plans, builds and operates solar and other renewable plants, with projects in Spain.
markets: Based in Barcelona; customers are utilities and corporate buyers. Other markets are unverified and no expansion plans are known.
rationale: B2B renewable producer with no consumer brand; Barcelona and Madrid races offer local hospitality, but marketing need is small.

name: ENGIE North America
desc: US arm of French group ENGIE, developing renewables, battery storage, retail energy and energy services for corporate and municipal clients.
markets: Operates in the United States, Canada and Mexico; customers include corporate and municipal clients.
rationale: Subsidiary of a global energy group with corporate customers; hospitality could support client relations, though sponsorship decisions sit with the parent.

name: First Gen
desc: Philippine power generator with gas-fired plants, geothermal assets through Energy Development Corporation and hydro, part of the Lopez Group.
markets: Power plants in the Philippines selling to utilities and distributors; no international operations.
rationale: Listed Philippine generator with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship has little commercial purpose.

name: Golden Energy and Resources
desc: Singapore-listed company controlled by Indonesia's Widjaja family, mainly producing and selling thermal coal in Indonesia through its subsidiary Borneo Indobara.
markets: Coal mining in Indonesia, sold to Asian customers; controlled by Sinar Mas family interests.
rationale: Coal producer with commodity customers and reputational limits on sponsorship; Singapore Grand Prix offers only generic corporate hospitality.

name: HD Hyundai Marine Solution
desc: Provides ship repair, retrofit, engine and environmental services for ship owners, as part of the HD Hyundai shipbuilding group.
markets: Marine services for ship owners worldwide, with South Korea as its base within HD Hyundai.
rationale: B2B marine services arm of a large group; F1 could support shipping client hospitality, though brand marketing needs are small.

name: Ignitis Group
desc: Lithuania's state-controlled energy company with Baltic electricity and gas networks, wind and pumped-storage generation, and power and gas supply.
markets: Operations in Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Poland and Finland serving households, businesses and industry.
rationale: State-controlled energy group with consumer brands but regional scope; F1 fit is modest.

name: Pacific Fusion
desc: Develops pulsed-power fusion systems for commercial electricity generation, founded in 2023 and launched with a large Series A round.
markets: Research and development in the United States; pre-revenue, with no commercial fusion plants operating yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue fusion startup; technology showcase appeal exists, but early stage and research focus make F1 a weak fit.

name: Permanent Power Company
desc: Power platform focused on energy, according to Crunchbase; no location, products or customers are given.
markets: No location is given; products, customers and any international activity are unknown.
rationale: Nothing is known about its business or customers, so F1 fit cannot be established.

name: RSK Group
desc: UK privately owned environmental, engineering and technical consultancy offering geotechnical, energy, infrastructure, laboratory and renewable services.
markets: Offices and projects in the United Kingdom, Europe and other regions serving public and private sector clients.
rationale: B2B consultancy with international client base; F1 hospitality and sustainability themes could help win and entertain clients.

name: SDIC Power Holdings
desc: Power producer running hydro, coal, wind and solar plants in China and overseas; unit of State Development and Investment Corporation.
markets: Plants in China plus overseas projects; sells electricity to grids. Parent is a Chinese state investment group.
rationale: State-owned generator with grid customers and no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak despite the Chinese Grand Prix.
